status: DRAFT for working-group review (30 Nov - 4 Dec 2026). Not validated.
question: Can this country plan, produce or adapt, and use trustworthy guidelines, and which strategy should it choose next: develop from scratch or contextualise existing guidelines?
principle: Function over paper: a document that says something exists scores nothing on its own.

scale.source: Adapted from WHO (2023) Supporting the routine use of evidence during the policy-making process: a WHO checklist, pp. 22-33, and PAHO (2023) Handbook, p. 40

levels.label: Awareness
levels.description: The need is recognised; nothing in place yet.

levels.label: Development
levels.description: First structures and practices, isolated or person-dependent, often project-funded.

levels.label: Assessment
levels.description: Accepted and running, but structures and rules can still be changed or dissolved easily.

levels.label: Maturation
levels.description: Routine and taken for granted: legal mandate, sustainable funding, retained capacity; survives change of government.

special.label: No evidence
special.description: Not scorable from the evidence available. Shown, never treated as 0.

special.label: Not applicable
special.description: Does not apply to this country's system (e.g. subnational uptake in a small centralised system).

domains.title: Mandate and governance
domains.definition: The legal and institutional basis that makes guideline work a standing government function: who is mandated, through which binding instrument, and whether it survives changes of government.

subdomains.title: Legal mandate
subdomains.definition: A law or decree that assigns guideline work to a public body.

questions.text: Which law or decree mandates guidelines, and in which section?
Does it name the body responsible?
When was it enacted?

subdomains.title: Operational instrument
subdomains.definition: The binding order, manual or regulation that turns the mandate into a working process.

questions.text: Which instrument operationalises the mandate (order, manual, regulation), and when was it issued?
How many times has it been reissued or replaced, and why?
Does it specify steps, roles and timelines, or only principles?

anchors.0: No instrument; the need is recognised.
anchors.1: A first order or manual exists; the process runs ad hoc or as a project.
anchors.2: The order is in force and has run at least one full cycle, but it is still being reissued or restructured.
anchors.3: Stable through at least one change of government, built into planning, revised only after an evaluation.

subdomains.title: Designated entity
subdomains.definition: A named unit that runs the programme, with staff and decision rights.

questions.text: Which unit runs the programme, and where does it sit in the ministry?
Can it approve or reject a guideline, or only advise?
How many staff does it have?

subdomains.title: Editorial independence
subdomains.definition: Protection of recommendations from political or commercial pressure.

questions.text: Does any rule protect recommendations from being changed by the ministry or funders after the panel decides?
Has a recommendation ever been overridden, and how was it handled?

subdomains.title: Continuity
subdomains.definition: The programme keeps running across changes of minister or government.

questions.text: Has the programme survived at least one change of government?
Which stage is it in: being set up, partly routine, or fully routine (PAHO's three institutionalisation phases)?

subdomains.title: Participation in governance
subdomains.definition: Who outside the ministry sits in the programme's decisions.

questions.text: Which societies, academic bodies, payers and patient groups have a formal seat?
Are subnational health authorities represented?

subdomains.title: Political commitment
subdomains.definition: Visible, sustained backing for the programme from senior decision makers.

questions.text: Do national health strategies or plans name the guideline programme as a priority?
Has a minister or senior official publicly backed it, or defended a recommendation under pressure?
Did that backing continue after the last change of leadership?

domains.title: Financing
domains.definition: The money that pays for guideline work: how much, from where, how stable, and through how many channels.

subdomains.title: Dedicated budget
subdomains.definition: A budget line for guideline development and updating.

questions.text: Is there a named budget line, and how much was allocated in each of the last three years?
How many guidelines did that fund per year?

subdomains.title: Stability
subdomains.definition: Funding that does not depend on one minister, one project or one donor.

questions.text: Is the budget recurrent or project-based?
What share comes from external donors or development partners?

subdomains.title: Source integrity
subdomains.definition: Funding sources that cannot steer recommendations.

questions.text: Does any industry money reach guideline development directly or through societies?
Are all funding sources published for each guideline?

subdomains.title: Funding channels
subdomains.definition: How money reaches developers, and how many developers can receive it.

questions.text: Through how many institutions can public guideline money flow?
Can private or non-government developers be contracted?
What happens to the pipeline if the main channel stalls?

domains.title: Priority setting
domains.definition: How a country decides which guidelines to develop or update, and whether the chosen topics match the population's needs rather than who nominated them.

subdomains.title: Process and criteria
subdomains.definition: A documented, repeatable method with explicit criteria and weights.

questions.text: Is there a written prioritisation method, and which criteria and weights does it use?
Was it based on an existing tool (WHO criteria, PRIO, PriGPC, NICE)?
How often is the list reviewed?

subdomains.title: Topic sources
subdomains.definition: Who can put a topic on the long list.

questions.text: Who nominated topics in the last cycle, by type (societies, industry, hospitals, ministry programmes, public)?
Can industry nominate?
Are topics also generated from burden data, not only nominations?

subdomains.title: Evidence used for scoring
subdomains.definition: Who supplies the information the scorers rely on.

questions.text: Is the evidence for each topic compiled by an independent secretariat or by the nominator?
What counts as acceptable evidence (peer-reviewed data only, or also position papers and news)?

subdomains.title: Decision makers
subdomains.definition: Who scores and approves the list, and how many people judge each topic.

questions.text: How many people sit on the committee, and from which organisations?
How many people score each topic before the plenary?
What vote counts as consensus?

subdomains.title: Fit to need
subdomains.definition: Whether the final list matches the burden of disease across age groups and populations.

questions.text: What share of the top 20 causes of death and disability have a current national guideline or a slot on the agenda?
How are children, rare diseases and vulnerable groups represented on the list?

subdomains.title: Link to funding and research
subdomains.definition: Whether a priority actually gets funded, and whether evidence gaps feed a research agenda.

questions.text: What share of prioritised topics were funded and started on schedule?
Are evidence gaps found during prioritisation passed to a national research agenda?

domains.title: Workforce and production capacity
domains.definition: The people and institutions able to develop or adapt guidelines to standard, how many there are, and how concentrated they are.

subdomains.title: Methodologists
subdomains.definition: People trained to run systematic reviews, GRADE (the standard method for rating evidence certainty) and panel processes.

questions.text: How many people in the country have led or co-led a guideline to standard in the last five years?
Has anyone mapped this capacity, and when?

subdomains.title: Institutions
subdomains.definition: Organisations that can deliver a complete guideline.

questions.text: How many institutions can deliver a guideline end to end?
What share of national guidelines in the last five years came from the single largest one?

subdomains.title: Specialised skills
subdomains.definition: Skills beyond methods: equity analysis, costing, conflict-of-interest management, patient engagement.

questions.text: How many developers have experience with equity analysis, costing and managing conflicts of interest?
Are health economists involved routinely?

subdomains.title: Training pipeline
subdomains.definition: How new methodologists and panel contributors are trained, rewarded and kept.

questions.text: Is there a recurring training course or degree track?
How many people completed it in the last three years?
How is staff turnover handled?
How are contributors' time and work recognised: payment, continuing-education credits, authorship, or protected time from their employer?

subdomains.title: Throughput
subdomains.definition: What the system produces per year against its plan.

questions.text: How many guidelines were published or updated per year in the last three years?
How does that compare with the planned number?

domains.title: Methods, evidence and contextualisation track record
domains.definition: The standard methods a country uses, the evidence and local data it can reach, and its record of developing, adopting or adapting guidelines. This domain carries the tool's core output: whether to develop from scratch or contextualise.

subdomains.title: Methods standard
subdomains.definition: A national manual that sets how guidelines are made, adopted or adapted.

questions.text: Is there a national methods manual, and when was it last updated?
Does it cover adoption and adaptation (for example GRADE-ADOLOPMENT), or only development from scratch?

subdomains.title: Access to evidence
subdomains.definition: Access to databases, full texts and existing guidelines from other countries and WHO.

questions.text: Do developers have institutional access to the main bibliographic databases?
Is there a routine search of existing international guidelines before a new one starts?

subdomains.title: Local data
subdomains.definition: Country data on burden, costs, practice variation and values, used to contextualise.

questions.text: Which local data sources were used in the last three guidelines (burden, cost, practice, patient values)?
Where data were missing, what was used instead?

subdomains.title: Contextualisation history
subdomains.definition: The country's record of adopting or adapting existing guidelines, and what came of it.

questions.text: How many national guidelines in the last five years were developed from scratch, adopted or adapted?
For adapted ones, which source guidelines were used and what was changed?
Were any adaptations later abandoned, and why?

subdomains.title: Quality of output
subdomains.definition: Whether finished guidelines meet an appraisal standard.

questions.text: Are national guidelines appraised with AGREE II (the standard guideline appraisal instrument), and what threshold must they pass?
What share passed in the last cycle?
What share of appraised guidelines came through the national priority list?

subdomains.title: Updating
subdomains.definition: A process for keeping guidelines current.

questions.text: Is there a set review interval?
What share of national guidelines is older than five years without review?

domains.title: Integrity: conflicts of interest and transparency
domains.definition: The rules and practice that keep recommendations free of undue influence, and make the process visible to anyone outside it.

subdomains.title: Conflict-of-interest policy
subdomains.definition: A written rule for declaring, classifying and managing interests.

questions.text: Is there a written policy, reviewed by a body independent of the panel?
How does it classify financial versus non-financial interests?

subdomains.title: Conflict-of-interest practice
subdomains.definition: What actually happens to people who declare interests.

questions.text: In the last cycle, how many declared interests led to exclusion or recusal, and how many to disclosure only?
How are indirect ties classified, such as a member's society partnering with a company?

subdomains.title: Role separation
subdomains.definition: Keeping those who propose a topic from controlling its recommendations.

questions.text: Can the person or body that nominated a topic sit on that guideline's steering committee or panel?
If so, under what limits?

subdomains.title: Public disclosure
subdomains.definition: Publication of methods, panel members, interests and funding for every guideline.

questions.text: For each national guideline, are panel members, declared interests and funding published?
Is there a public repository of national guidelines?

subdomains.title: Appeals and external review
subdomains.definition: A route for outsiders to challenge priorities or recommendations.

questions.text: Is there public consultation before final approval?
How many appeals were received in the last cycle, and how many changed anything?

domains.title: Link to decisions and payment
domains.definition: Whether guidelines decide something that matters: what insurers pay for, what the essential medicines list contains, what health technology assessment recommends, and what facilities are licensed or accredited against.

subdomains.title: Payer linkage
subdomains.definition: Benefit packages or reimbursement rules that cite national guidelines.

questions.text: Which benefit packages or payment rules cite a national guideline?
Must facilities adopt the guideline's pathway to be paid?

subdomains.title: Medicines and technology decisions
subdomains.definition: Two-way links between guidelines, the essential medicines list and health technology assessment.

questions.text: Do health technology assessments use national guidelines to define standard of care?
Has an assessment ever triggered a guideline update, or the reverse?

subdomains.title: Regulation and accreditation
subdomains.definition: Guidelines used as standards in licensing, accreditation or quality programmes.

questions.text: Do licensing or accreditation standards require adherence to national guidelines?
Is adherence audited?

subdomains.title: Reach of the link
subdomains.definition: How many facilities and patients the link actually binds.

questions.text: How many facilities are contracted under guideline-linked packages?
What share of the target population can reach them?

subdomains.title: Lobbying exposure
subdomains.definition: Protection against capture once guidelines decide money.

questions.text: Where a guideline drives reimbursement, are its panel's conflicts reviewed more strictly?
Is there a rule separating payer negotiations from panel decisions?

domains.title: Implementation and reach
domains.definition: How guidelines get from the national level into practice in regions and facilities, and how widely they are known and used.

subdomains.title: National implementation policy
subdomains.definition: A plan that comes with each guideline: who owns implementation after release, and with what resources.

questions.text: Does each national guideline ship with an implementation plan and budget?
Who owns implementation after release, beyond dissemination?

subdomains.title: Subnational uptake
subdomains.definition: Regional or local health authorities adopting national guidelines into their own programmes.

questions.text: Do regional or local authorities have a mechanism to adopt national guidelines?
In a devolved system, can they ignore them?

subdomains.title: Facility uptake
subdomains.definition: Hospitals and clinics turning guidelines into local pathways.

questions.text: What share of facilities have a written pathway based on a national guideline for priority conditions?
Is there any measure of adherence?

subdomains.title: Dissemination and tools
subdomains.definition: Formats that reach users: summaries, apps, training, a public repository.

questions.text: Through which channels are guidelines disseminated?
Is use of these channels measured?

subdomains.title: Barriers
subdomains.definition: Systematic identification of what blocks use, such as drugs not stocked or not covered.

questions.text: Are barriers assessed before or after release?
Has a recommendation been changed because it could not be implemented?

subdomains.title: Professional trust and acceptance
subdomains.definition: Whether clinicians and managers see national guidelines as credible and their own.

questions.text: Has any survey measured clinicians' awareness of and trust in national guidelines?
Do professional societies endorse national guidelines, or issue competing ones on the same topic?
Are national guidelines taught in medical and nursing curricula?

domains.title: Monitoring, evaluation and evidence generation
domains.definition: Whether the programme measures its own performance and effect, learns from it, and generates the local evidence its guidelines lack.

subdomains.title: Programme indicators
subdomains.definition: A defined set of structure, process and outcome indicators for the programme.

questions.text: Which indicators are tracked (guidelines funded, published, on time, money spent)?
Are they reported publicly, and how often?

subdomains.title: Adherence and outcomes
subdomains.definition: Measurement of whether guidelines change practice and health results.

questions.text: Has adherence to any national guideline been measured in the last five years?
Has any outcome change been attributed to a guideline?

subdomains.title: Programme evaluation
subdomains.definition: Periodic external review of the programme as a whole.

questions.text: Has the programme been evaluated independently, and when?
What changed as a result?

subdomains.title: Research agenda link
subdomains.definition: A national research agenda that targets the evidence gaps guidelines expose.

questions.text: Is there a national research-for-health agenda, and does it list guideline evidence gaps?
Does it meet PAHO's checklist for research agendas?

subdomains.title: Learning loop
subdomains.definition: Lessons fed back into methods, priorities and governance.

questions.text: When the programme's orders or methods were revised, was the revision based on an evaluation?
Is there a documented lessons-learned process?

scoring.unknown: dropped from means, listed, reflected in coverage and in the sensitivity range (unknowns at 0 and at 3)
scoring.status: Proposed 22 Nov 2026; to be confirmed by the working group
